decision.rationale: A stopped sedan occupies the ego lane far enough ahead to place closest approach after trace startup while late avoidance creates a critical, collision-free rear-end threat.
The hostable hazard models the moving lead braking hard while ego follows closely, with late but collision-avoiding ego response; the unmodeled trailing tailgater is contextual.
Model the cut-out reveal as late avoidance release toward a genuinely stopped lead, with sufficient speed and gap for a critical non-contact response.

A slow vehicle emerges into an ordinary uncontrolled junction shortly before ego arrives, using the generic junction control because explicit obstruction and uncontrolled-junction parameters are unavailable.

A slow van emerges at an ordinary uncontrolled-compatible junction almost concurrently with ego, lingering near the conflict point while late avoidance creates a close non-collision encounter; explicit obstruction modeling is unavailable.
At an all-way-stop junction, both vehicles proceed after stopping and reach the shared conflict area in close succession.
At an all-way-stop junction, both vehicles proceed after stopping, with the challenger entering only slightly before ego so their paths pass within the critical conflict area.
Use the hostable bus-shelter occlusion proxy so a walking adult is genuinely hidden and then emerges into the ego lane with enough late-reaction margin to become critical without forcing contact.
Model the pedestrian's hesitation as a slow, delayed roadside crossing that resumes into the ego lane with late ego avoidance, preserving a critical but non-contact conflict.
An oncoming cyclist rides against traffic into the ego lane with sufficient closing distance for a late, critical, collision-free avoidance response.
A solved lane-closure taper shifts a slower adjacent-lane vehicle into the ego lane late enough to create a critical but avoidable merge conflict.
A compact solved lane-closure taper forces a slower adjacent-lane van to merge shortly before the ego arrives, creating a late but avoidable braking conflict.

A barrier-and-plant work area partially closes the running lane near an ordinary corridor junction, forcing a lateral shift as an adult flagger steps into the open lane with a late but non-contact avoidance window.

A compact barrier-and-plant closure occupies only part of the running lane near an ordinary corridor junction, while an adult flagger steps into the shifted traffic path late enough to demand firm non-contact braking.
Model the unavailable animal actor as a compact roadside VRU crossing into the ego lane with late but collision-avoiding ego response.
A stopped box truck represents a hazard revealed just beyond a crest or curve, with a high-speed approach and delayed avoidance creating a critical but non-contact rear-end conflict.
An oncoming sedan drifts across the centreline on an ordinary corridor bend, creating a late high-closing-speed conflict while retaining enough avoidance time to prevent contact.

An oncoming sedan starts farther away and encroaches across the centreline late on an ordinary corridor bend, delaying closest approach while producing a close, braking-demanding encounter with recoverable avoidance time.
A wrong-way sedan approaches head-on in the ego lane with summed closing speed and late but collision-avoiding ego response.
A parked sedan reverses from a kerbside space into the ego lane with late avoidance release, creating a critical but non-contact conflict on an ordinary corridor.
Represent the double-parked delivery vehicle as a stationary box truck blocking the ego lane on an ordinary corridor, with a late but collision-avoiding response.
Represent the released children with one child pedestrian entering from the roadside on an ordinary hostable corridor, timed for a late but collision-free crossing conflict.
A box truck braking hard is the nearest hostable proxy for the sudden longitudinal hazard created when cargo falls from a truck ahead.
Because the available maps have no roundabouts, an ordinary junction hosts a vehicle crossing the ego's intended exit path with a close, collision-free arrival.

Because the maps lack roundabouts, the circulating vehicle is represented as an adjacent-lane vehicle cutting across the ego path on an ordinary corridor, with a wider initial gap for delayed development and a late but collision-avoiding response.
A cyclist emerges from behind parked vehicles and crosses the ego lane with late but collision-avoiding ego reaction.
Model the double-parked truck with the nearest supported vehicle-like roadside occluder, revealing a walking adult late enough for a critical but collision-free crossing conflict.
Approximate the unsupported spin dynamics as a sudden lateral incursion by a slower sedan into the ego lane, with late avoidance calibrated for a critical but collision-free encounter.
A moving sedan traveling at half the ego speed creates a Euro NCAP CCRm closing conflict, with late avoidance yielding a critical but collision-free near approach.
Represent the two-vehicle weave as an adjacent-lane sedan cutting across the ego on an ordinary high-speed corridor, with late avoidance producing a critical but non-contact encounter.
A slower vehicle in an adjacent lane cuts across the ego lane toward an exit, creating a late but avoidable lateral conflict.
A vehicle approaching from the left reaches the junction shortly before the left-turning ego, creating a late but avoidable crossing conflict.
A slower, large vehicle approaching from the left reaches the junction just before the left-turning ego, producing a late close-clearance conflict while preserving time for collision-free braking.
The ego turns left at an ordinary junction across an oncoming motorcycle timed to reach the conflict point shortly before the ego, with late avoidance preserving a critical near miss without contact.

The ego turns left at an ordinary junction across a slower oncoming motorcycle timed to clear the conflict point only shortly before ego arrival, producing a late close encounter while broad corridor eligibility improves portability.
Model the pedestrian emerging from behind the reversing vehicle as an occluded roadside crossing behind a covered car, preserving the hide-then-reveal pedestrian conflict on hostable corridors.
A cyclist enters from the nearside shortly before the ego reaches a close ordinary-corridor conflict, with late avoidance calibrated to create a critical non-contact encounter.
Barriers close part of the ego lane through a work area, forcing a narrowed running path as a road worker steps into it late enough to create a critical but avoidable conflict.

A short, modest-width barrier closure narrows the ego lane while a worker steps into the remaining running path with limited warning, producing late braking demand without requiring an unplaceably narrow route.
Because the available maps have no rail crossings, a moving lead braking hard on an ordinary high-speed corridor is the nearest hostable surrogate for traffic stopping when a crossing activates.
A pedestrian unexpectedly emerges from behind a covered roadside vehicle and occupies the running lane shortly before the ego arrives.
Represent the yellow-light dilemma as a late-released signalized-junction conflict, with cross traffic clearing shortly before ego arrival to create a critical but collision-free encounter.

Model the yellow-light dilemma as a late-revealed signalized-junction conflict with slower cross traffic arriving just ahead of ego, producing close clearance and braking demand while retaining a collision-free margin.
A van representing an emergency vehicle enters the signalized junction under abrupt preemption shortly before ego reaches the conflict point, forcing late collision-free avoidance.

A van representing an emergency vehicle enters a signalized junction under abrupt preemption just before ego, with reduced cross-traffic speed and tight arrival timing producing a late, close, collision-free conflict.
Because rail crossings are unavailable, a lead vehicle braking hard for a newly restrictive control on an ordinary corridor is the nearest hostable proxy for a descending level-crossing barrier.

Because the available maps have no roundabouts, this uses an ordinary junction where a conflicting vehicle arrives shortly before the ego, preserving the intended entering-versus-circulating conflict.

Because the maps lack roundabouts, an ordinary junction hosts a tightly timed entering-versus-conflicting-vehicle encounter, with lower approach speeds delaying closest approach and broad corridor eligibility improving portability.
Because the available maps have no roundabouts, this hosts the exit-crossing hazard as a pedestrian entering the ego lane from the roadside on an ordinary corridor.
Represent the unavailable roundabout as a bicycle crossing on a circulating-like conflicting path at an ordinary junction, timed for a close non-contact encounter after late ego avoidance.

Represent the unavailable roundabout as a cyclist crossing the ego path on an ordinary corridor, with a distant conflict anchor for sufficient ego travel and late release for a close non-contact encounter.
A cyclist initiates a left turn at an ordinary junction and crosses the ego lane shortly before ego reaches the conflict point, with late avoidance preserving a critical non-contact near miss.

A cyclist initiates a leftward crossing from the roadside into the ego lane on an ordinary corridor, with a distant conflict anchor ensuring sufficient ego travel and tightly timed late avoidance producing a critical non-contact encounter.
A filtering motorcycle moving ahead of ego brakes hard on an ordinary high-speed corridor, creating a late but collision-avoidable rear-end conflict.
A slow cargo bicycle is modeled as a moving lead occupying the ego lane on the nearest hostable ordinary corridor, with late ego reaction tuned for a critical but collision-free close approach.
A slow box truck enters just ahead of ego and remains within the junction box, forcing a late but collision-free braking response.
A creeping box truck enters shortly before ego and continues to occupy the junction box, creating a delayed close encounter that requires firm but collision-free braking.
A slowly turning box truck crosses the ego path at an ordinary junction, with its long body and off-tracking rear creating a late but avoidable conflict.
A slowly turning box truck crosses closely ahead at an ordinary junction, leaving its off-tracking rear in the ego path late enough to demand hard but collision-free braking.
A stop-controlled challenger yields late and partially encroaches into the ego path, creating a critical junction conflict while preserving time for collision-free avoidance.
A slow vehicle yields late and encroaches through an ordinary junction just ahead of ego, producing a close, delayed conflict with late but collision-free avoidance.
Host the school-context brief on an ordinary corridor, using a covered car to represent the queued vehicles that genuinely hide the child until a late but avoidable crossing conflict.
Represent the unsupported child-on-scooter and school setting as a faster-moving child VRU entering an ordinary hostable corridor from the roadside.
A kerbside bus pulls into the running lane during the ego's pass on an ordinary high-speed corridor, approximating the unhostable school-bus setting while preserving a late, collision-free conflict.
A kerbside bus pulls into the running lane late during the ego's pass, with a larger initial gap delaying closest approach and broadly permissive corridor speeds improving portability.

A slower vehicle ahead in the adjacent lane loses lateral control as if oversteering on a bend and abruptly incurs into the ego lane, with late ego avoidance calibrated to produce a critical non-contact encounter.
A moving lead sedan brakes hard and loses longitudinal stability, proxying a wet-surface slide while preserving a late, collision-free rear-end conflict.
Represent the unmodeled gravel-induced loss of traction as a late-arriving vehicle crossing from an ordinary junction mouth into the ego vehicle's path.
Represent the unmodeled gravel-induced traction loss at an ordinary junction mouth as a moderately slower vehicle making a late lateral incursion into the ego lane.

A stopped bicycle is the closest hostable low-profile static-obstruction surrogate for a ladder lying across the ego lane, with a high enough ego speed and delayed reaction to produce a critical collision-free encounter.
A low-speed kerbside vehicle pullout is the nearest hostable proxy for a parked vehicle door intruding into the ego lane.
A solved temporary lane closure represents the spilled load narrowing an ordinary corridor, forcing a lateral shift while a slow worker provides the hostable critical conflict.
A compact solved lane closure represents the spilled load blocking most of the lane, while a late-revealed slow worker creates braking demand during the required lateral shift.
A covered parked-vehicle occluder represents the van, hiding an adult pedestrian until a late reveal on an ordinary high-speed corridor while preserving enough reaction margin to avoid contact.
Approximate the unsupported turning-truck sight obstruction with a covered-vehicle occluder that genuinely hides and then reveals oncoming bicycle traffic crossing the ego lane.
A bus shelter genuinely hides a walking adult until shortly before they enter the ego lane, producing a late but collision-free crossing conflict.
An oncoming sedan drifts across the centerline while cutting a bend apex, creating a late but avoidable closing-speed conflict.
An oncoming sedan cuts across the centerline near a bend apex after a longer approach, producing a late, close, but avoidable closing-speed conflict.
A moderately paced oncoming sedan drifts across the centreline late enough to create a critical combined-closing-speed conflict while preserving time for collision-free ego avoidance.

A slower oncoming sedan starts farther away so the encounter develops after 2.5 seconds, then drifts across the centreline late enough to produce a close, braking-demanding but avoidable conflict on ordinary corridors.
An oncoming box truck overtaking into the ego lane creates a late-revealed head-on conflict with sufficient post-warm-up time for collision-free evasive action.

A more distant, moderately slower oncoming box truck begins its overtaking encroachment late enough to produce a post-warm-up close head-on conflict while preserving time for collision-free avoidance.
A parked sedan reverses from a kerbside bay across the ego lane with late avoidance release, creating a critical but non-contact conflict on an ordinary corridor.
A parked sedan reverses slowly from a kerbside bay shortly before ego arrives, with late avoidance release creating strong braking demand while retaining non-contact margin across ordinary corridors.
The nearest hostable mechanism models the reversing vehicle as a covered roadside vehicle that initially hides a pedestrian before the pedestrian walks behind it and into the ego lane.
Model the protruding badly parked vehicle as a stationary lead obstacle partially occupying the running lane, with delayed avoidance tuned for a critical but collision-free pass or stop.
An aggressive sedan overtakes from an adjacent lane and cuts sharply into the ego lane at close range, representing the safety-critical portion of weaving around the ego.

An aggressive SUV approaches from an adjacent lane and makes a late, close cut across the ego's path, capturing the critical incursion within a weaving maneuver while delaying closest approach beyond startup.
Because falling cargo is unsupported, a box truck ahead braking hard is the nearest hostable surrogate for the abrupt longitudinal hazard created by a shed object.
A moving lead vehicle deliberately brakes hard to a stop in the running lane, forcing a late but collision-free rear-end avoidance response.
A moving lead vehicle braking hard represents the nearest vehicle in a sequentially braking traffic chain while preserving a late, collision-free rear-end conflict.
A moving box truck travels well below the ego speed, creating a sustained closing-speed rear-end conflict with late but collision-avoiding ego response.
A slower box truck merges from the adjacent lane into the ego lane at a late but non-contact-critical gap.
A low-speed sedan merges from a slip road into the ego lane with limited longitudinal clearance, prompting late collision avoidance without forcing contact.
A low-speed sedan merges from a slip road far enough ahead for the closing conflict to mature after 2.5 seconds, while late ego avoidance preserves a close, non-contact encounter.
A fast-moving adult pedestrian enters from the roadside and crosses the ego lane late enough to create a critical but avoidable conflict on an ordinary corridor.
A distracted adult pedestrian enters the ego lane shortly before arrival, forcing late collision-free braking on an ordinary corridor.
A solved lane closure shifts ego laterally around an excavation while a worker enters the running lane late enough to create a critical but avoidable conflict.

A placeable partial lane closure shifts ego laterally around an excavation while a worker enters the narrowed running lane with sufficiently late reveal and reaction timing to produce a critical avoidable conflict.
Model the construction plant as a slow box truck crossing from the solved lane-closure works area into the running carriageway, with late ego avoidance tuned for a critical non-contact encounter.

Model the construction plant as a slow box truck crossing from a compact, fully placeable lane-closure area into the running lane, with a shorter event lead and later ego reaction to create critical braking demand without forcing contact.
